capture_note: A DATED CAPTURE of a public lookup, not a live report and not a sandbox result. It observes nothing about what any file does.
warning: This is what the lookup showed at the capture time below. The live result may differ today — a report may now exist, or the detection counts may have changed. Neither outcome changes the answer to the question this artifact supports: a lookup result is not the evidence your conclusion rests on.

observed_result.note: No account was used, nothing was submitted, and no analysis was requested. The service simply has no record of this hash.

what_this_supports: No engine on this service had a verdict on record for this hash at the capture time.
The file had not been submitted to this service by anyone before the capture time.
what_this_does_not_support: That the file is safe. A service with no record of a file has not examined it, and 'not examined' is not 'examined and found clean'.
That the file is malicious. This result carries no verdict in either direction.
Anything about what the file does. This service aggregates verdicts from other engines; it is not an observation of behaviour.
Anything about the incident. The behaviour evidence is the SBX-K42 sandbox report and the SR-DEV-077 endpoint traces, and it stays that way whatever this lookup shows.
why_absence_is_not_evidence: A file that nobody has ever uploaded looks exactly like a file that is harmless, because in both cases there is nothing to display. A newly built package used against one organisation is the ordinary case for the first: it is unknown because it is new and narrow, not because it is safe. Reading an empty result as a clean bill of health is the specific error this mission exists to catch.
safety: Uploading a file to a public service shares it with third parties and cannot be undone. That habit matters far more outside this room than in it.
